'''Olaf Dreyer''' (born 1969, [[Hamburg]]) is a German [[theoretical physicist]] whose research interests include [[quantum gravity]] and the [[quantum measurement problem]]. Dreyer received his Ph.D. in quantum gravity in 2001 from the [[Pennsylvania State University]]<ref>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.houghtonmifflinbooks.com/booksellers/press_release/smolin/#physicists
 | title = Press release for "The Trouble with Physics" published by Houghton Mifflin Company: Hot Young Physicists
 | access-date = 22 January 2011
}}</ref> under the direction of [[Abhay Ashtekar]].<ref>{{cite web
 | last = Baez | first = John
 | title = This Week's Finds in Mathematical Physics (Week 189)
 | year = 2002
 | url = http://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/week189.html
 | access-date = 22 January 2011
}}</ref> Subsequently, he has held a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] in [[Waterloo, Ontario]], a Marie Curie Fellowship at [[Imperial College]], London, and a postdoctoral fellowship at the [[MIT Center for Theoretical Physics|Center for Theoretical Physics]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].

In 2002 Dreyer proposed<ref>{{citation
 | title = Quasinormal Modes, the Area Spectrum, and Black Hole Entropy
 | last = Dreyer | first = Olaf
 | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett.
 | volume = 90
 | issue = 8 | article-number = 081301
 | year = 2003
 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.081301
 | id = 
| pmid=12633415
| arxiv=gr-qc/0211076v1
| bibcode=2003PhRvL..90h1301D
}}</ref> a connection between the [[Immirzi parameter|Barbero-Immirzi parameter]] in [[loop quantum gravity]] and the asymptotic behaviour of [[black hole]] quasinormal modes (in numerical general relativity), building on previous insights due to Shahar Hod.<ref>{{citation
 | title = Bohr's Correspondence Principle and The Area Spectrum of Quantum Black Holes
 | last = Hod | first = Shahar
 | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett.
 | volume = 81
 | issue = 20 | pages = 4293–4296
 | year = 1998
 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.4293
 | id = 
| arxiv=gr-qc/9812002v2
| bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.4293H
}}</ref>  Subsequently, [[Lubos Motl]] proved that the exact asymptotic behaviour of the quasinormal modes of the Schwarzschild black hole was as predicted numerically.<ref>{{citation
 | title = An analytical computation of asymptotic Schwarzschild quasinormal frequencies
 | last = Motl | first = Lubos
 | journal = Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 
 | volume = 6 
 | issue = 6 | year = 2003
 | pages = 1135–1162
 | id = 
| arxiv=gr-qc/0212096v3
|bibcode = 2002gr.qc....12096M | doi = 10.4310/ATMP.2002.v6.n6.a3 }}</ref>

Dreyer has developed an approach to quantum gravity known as "internal relativity".<ref>{{citation
 | title = Knowing the mind of God: Seven theories of everything
 | last = Marshall | first = Michael
 | date = 4 March 2010
 | journal = New Scientist
 | url = https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn18612-knowing-the-mind-of-god-seven-theories-of-everything.html
}}</ref>
